item.title: AI Licensing Comes Full Circle
item.description: Aalok Mehta discusses the Trump administration’s recent interest in licensing frontier models, arguing that important implementation details remain unresolved since the idea was floated publicly in 2023.

item.title: Beyond Russian Gas: Trade-Offs in EU Liquefied Natural Gas Diversification
item.description: With Qatari LNG sidelined and U.S. supply poised to dominate Europe's gas market, a new CSIS analysis examines the trade-offs between American dependence and supplier diversification across three dimensions: geopolitical risk, price volatility, and supplier concentration.

item.title: What did the Trump-Xi Summit Achieve?
item.description: The U.S.-China summit was expected to cover trade, investment, the war with Iran, and Taiwan. CSIS’s leading China experts assessed its outcomes in a special live episode of State of Play.

item.title: Why China Is Now a Peer Competitor to the United States in Cyberspace
item.description: China has matured its cyber ecosystem in sophistication, scale, stealth, and strategy—now rivaling, and in some areas surpassing, the United States. Washington should use the window following Trump's Beijing visit to strengthen its response to China's cyber threat.

item.title: Bitter Harvest: Diagnosing and Deterring Chinese Coercive Agricultural Trade Restrictions
item.description: Beijing is increasingly deploying agricultural import restrictions for geopolitical ends. By diagnosing which industries are most exposed to these restrictions, countries can design and implement risk mitigation strategies that improve resilience to coercive threats.

item.title: The Killing of Abu-Bilal al-Minuki and the U.S. Military’s Deepening Involvement in Nigeria
item.description: On Friday, May 15, U.S. and Nigerian forces killed an Islamic State leader the president described as the group's "second in command." But who was he? And why were U.S. forces involved in combat operations in Nigeria?

item.title: CDC Director’s Nomination Is an Opportunity to Reconstitute the CDC
item.description: With the nomination of Dr. Erica Schwartz to be director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, a window has opened to repair the agency, reconstitute it to meet new realities, and regain essential bipartisan trust and confidence among the American people.

item.title: Foreign Investment Attraction and CFIUS: Can the “Known Investor Program” Make U.S. Investment Screening More Efficient?
item.description: Associate Fellow Andrea Leonard Palazzi reviews the goals and design of CFIUS’s Known Investor Program through the perspectives of key stakeholders, identifying success factors for the program and implications for broader CFIUS reform.

item.title: How Trade Reduces the Risk of War
item.description: A new study demonstrates the quantifiable contributions of economic integration in building sustainable global security.

item.title: San Diego Mosque Shooting Marks a Deadly First in the United States
item.description: The shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego appears to be the first ideologically motivated lethal attack on a mosque in the United States this century.

item.title: Insights into the “Pay Now, Argue Later” Mechanism
item.description: The “pay now, argue later” tax administration scheme requires taxpayers to settle tax obligations before filing a complaint, which can introduce uncertainty and financial strain for investors, potentially discouraging both expansion and long-term investment.

item.title: States Weekly Newsletter: May 20, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers May 20, 2026.

item.title: A Summit of Equals
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch provides an overview of the Trump-Xi summit.

item.title: What the Trump-Xi Summit Revealed, and Left Unsaid, About U.S.-China Tech Competition
item.description: The Trump-Xi summit revealed how little progress has been made on the most consequential dimensions of U.S.-China competition: AI, cyber operations, export controls, and digital sovereignty. While trade dominated headlines, deeper technological tensions remain unresolved.

item.title: A New Supercarrier Emerges
item.description: China’s fourth aircraft carrier is rapidly taking shape at Dalian Shipyard. Satellite imagery reveals a vessel likely to be larger and more advanced than its predecessors, with evidence suggesting it may be China’s first nuclear-powered carrier.

item.title: Revisiting the Relationship Between Economic and Sea Power
item.description: Sea power begins with economic power. MAP and the SHIPS Act seek to rebuild the maritime industrial base—shipyards, mariners, logistics networks, and commercial fleets—that underpins U.S. naval strategy and will bolster U.S. maritime competitiveness against China.

item.title: Will the AI Economy Have a Middle Class? The Case for an AI Homestead Policy
item.description: Navin Girishankar argues that America needs an AI Homestead policy that offers the middle class a wages-to-wealth ladder for the coming AI economy. It is a commitment to upskilling, labor mobility, business formation, data as an asset, and community access to compute.

item.title: Testing the Future of Joint All-Domain Operations in Africa
item.description: Africa’s open terrain could become the proving ground for next-generation warfare, helping the U.S. and partners test drones, electronic warfare, and joint all-domain operations while signaling deterrence to China and Russia.

item.title: The Vatican Just Outmaneuvered Washington on AI
item.description: The Vatican’s AI intervention exposes Washington’s blind spot: Policymakers are debating hypothetical doomsday scenarios while missing the real crises already reshaping human dignity, work, truth, and power. Washington must move beyond abstract AGI fears and build a civil society dialogue on human dignity, supply chains, truth, and statecraft.

item.title: Global Terrorism Threat Assessment 2026
item.description: Terrorism is currently declining as a U.S. national security priority, and resources available for counterterrorism are decreasing accordingly. At the same time, uncertainty regarding the future of global terrorism is increasing, bringing greater risk of surprise.
